head: claude/sweep-ch02-sec2b-d618
title: Prove the uniform decay of homogeneous theta (Theorem 2.2.5.4(5)–(6))
body:
Proves both remaining statements of `RiemannMasullo/Ch02_AdelicTheta/Sec2b.lean`, Theorem 2.2.5.4(5)–(6), p. 98.

Closes #3523
Closes #3524

**Result: proved.** One new `private theorem`, `homogeneousAdelicTheta_decay_bounded_uniform`, placed above (5). It proves the threshold-one estimates by averaging the uniform theta bounds of Theorem 2.2.3.4(5) (`adelicTheta_decay_bounded_threshold_one`, Sec2a) over the norm-one idele classes, using the averaging helpers already in the file. For the two-sided bound with `ω₁ ≠ 1`, the polar term is zero and the large- and small-norm bounds are rewritten as exponentials in `|log ‖g‖|`. (6) is the private lemma, and (5) follows from it with `T = 1`. The lemma is needed because (5) comes before (6) in the file.

**On the earlier blocker** (the comments on #3523/#3524 about the instance paths of `IsVonNBounded`): the hypothesis types are in fact syntactically identical. The timeout comes from how the Sec2a lemma is applied. Applied to `B hB N` in one go, or inside `obtain … := lemma … hB N`, the unifier meets `hB` before the instance arguments are synthesized, unfolds the Schwartz–Bruhat instances, and runs out of heartbeats (47 s at 2M heartbeats). Applying it in steps with `have` (`have h₀ := lemma (F := F) B; have h₁ := h₀ hB N; obtain … := h₁`) elaborates instantly. A comment in the proof says so.

**Checks (all run locally):**
- `lake build RiemannMasullo.Ch02_AdelicTheta.Sec2b`: OK. Module time 69 s on `main`, 66 s with this change.
- `lake build` (full): `Build completed successfully (18842 jobs)`.
- `scripts/lint.sh`: `lint: ok`.
- `scripts/Signatures.lean` run on this module before and after (all 47 declarations), compared with `scripts/signatures.sh --compare`: no changes.
- `#print axioms` on both theorems: `[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The `sorryAx` comes only through the statements' own definitions: `adelePolarSubspace` and `homogeneousAdelicTheta_polarTerm` already show it, by way of `adeleSchwartzFourier` and the unproved `schwartzBruhat_fourier_continuousLinear` (AppD/Sec1c). The same holds for the proved neighbour `homogeneousAdelicTheta_decay_both`.
